<reason>Side B (PRO) won by constructing a more comprehensive affirmative case: enforceable rules civilize sovereignty by preventing beggar-thy-neighbor cascades, and workability is secured through a package of collective insurance (regional reserves, emergency financing), objective verification via a foods observatory, and targeted penalties that shield vulnerable populations while deterring defiance. Side A's skeptical case against enforceability was strong but defensive, and B successfully reframed A's evasion argument as a description of the status quo rather than a refutation of rules.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side B's Rebuttal 2 answers to pressure questions (A1/A2), which proposed the staple foods observatory for verification and targeted elite sanctions paired with solidarity mechanisms, effectively neutralizing Side A's enforcement dilemma.</best_rebuttal>
